headline: Lake and Summit Day Use Permits
reservation: While Mont-Orford generally allows walk-in entry, daily capacity limits apply to the popular beach areas and summit trails during summer and autumn. It is recommended to purchase the Sépaq daily passage online in advance to guarantee entry, as specific lots will close when full.

days.title: Lakeside Recreation and Beachfronts

stops.name: Stukely Lake
stops.detail: Utilize the boat rentals or beach area for water-based views of the surrounding peaks.

stops.name: Le Cavaliere Trail
stops.detail: A multi-use path suitable for seeing the transition from lake marshes to hardwood forests.

days.driving: Allow 20 minutes from Magog; traffic increases near Lake Stukely on weekends.
days.note: Beach water quality is monitored; check local signage for swimming status.

days.title: Glacial Landscapes and Bogs
days.start: Suggested: 8:30 AM from the Visitors Centre

stops.name: Étangs Fer-de-Lance
stops.detail: Walk the boardwalk over this protected bog to spot herons and specific wetland flora.

stops.name: Fraser Lake Sector
stops.detail: Explore the quieter northern side of the park for secluded picnic spots and secondary trailheads.

days.driving: Allow 30 minutes to transit between the Stukely and Fraser sectors.
days.note: Mosquito activity is high near the bogs in early summer; plan accordingly.

days.title: Peak Vistas and Ridge Walking
days.start: Suggested: 8 AM from the Le Cerisier Center

stops.name: Mont Chauve
stops.detail: Hike the ridge for a clear view across Lake Memphrémagog and the ski hills of Orford.

stops.name: Le Ruisseau-David
stops.detail: Follow the trail along the stream for a moderate ascent through mature maple groves.

days.driving: Local transit; conditions vary based on trailhead parking availability.
days.note: The Mont Chauve loop is a popular trek; mid-week visits offer a quieter experience.

intel.title: Beach vs Trailhead Lots
intel.text: Parking at Stukely Lake fills rapidly on hot summer days. Use the Le Cerisier sector lots for hiking access if the waterfront areas are congested.

intel.title: Reliable Corridor Coverage
intel.text: Cellular service is generally good throughout the park due to proximity to Magog, though it may dip in deep valleys. The summits usually offer strong signals.

intel.title: Magog Service Hub
intel.text: All major services and fuel stations are located in nearby Magog or Cherry River. There are no refueling stations inside the park's protected perimeter.

intel.title: Autumn Foliage Peak
intel.text: Late September to early October sees extreme volume for the 'Flambée des Couleurs'. Arrive very early or use shuttle services if offered by the local municipality.

intel.title: Multi-Sector Entry
intel.text: The park has two main entrances (Stukely and Fraser) that are not connected by an internal park road. Ensure your GPS is set to the specific sector required.

plan.arrival: Arrive at Montreal-Trudeau (YUL), drive east on Autoroute 10, and stock up in Magog before entering the park via the Cherry River gate.
plan.vehicle: Standard passenger vehicles are ideal; RVs should check specific site dimensions at the Stukely campground.
plan.goldenHour: The Mont Chauve belvedere offers expansive sunset views over the Appalachian plateau.
